The length of a rectangular prism is decreasing at a rate of $3\,\text{cm}\text{/min},$ the width is increasing at a rate of $5\,\text{cm}\text{/min},$ and the $5\,\text{cm}$ height does not change. How fast is the surface area of the rectangular prism decreasing when its dimensions are $3\,\text{cm}$ in length and $10\,\text{cm}$ in width?
question.worked_solution:
Let $x,y,z$ be the dimensions of the solid, and let $V$ be its volume. We are given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =3\,\text{cm}, \\ y & =10\,\text{cm}, \\ z & =5\,\text{cm}, \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =-3\,\text{cm}\text{/min}, \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =5\,\text{cm}\text{/min}.\end{aligned}
$$

We would like to find $\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t}.$

We want to find the rate of change of $S$ knowing the rate of change of $x$ and $y.$ So, we start with the formula for the surface area of the rectangular prism:

$$
S=2xz+2xy+2yz
$$

Since $z=5\,\text{cm}$ is not changing, we get

$$
S=10x+2xy+10y.
$$

Now, we differentiate with respect to time using the chain rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(10x+2xy+10y) \\ \frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t} & =(2x+10)(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})+(10+2y)(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}).\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plug in the known values into the above expression. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t} & =(2\cdot 3+10)(5)+(10+2\cdot 10)(-3) \\  & =80-90 \\  & =-10\,{\text{cm}}^{2}\text{/min}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface area of the rectangular prism is decreasing at a rate of $10\,{\text{cm}}^{2}/\text{min}.$
